name: Single-ended triode, high-mu
reference: 0 dBFS = grid swing of 1 V peak
source: Computed by examples/harmonics_presetgen.rs (static curve projected onto T2..T9): Koren triode model for 12AX7 (mu=100, ex=1.4, kg1=1060, kp=600, kvb=300); common cathode with resistive load, supply 300 V, plate load 100 kohm, fixed bias -1.5 V, grid swing +/-1 V peak = 0 dBFS (grid current ignored); quiescent plate 204.7 V at 0.95 mA; https://www.normankoren.com/Audio/Tubemodspice_article.html (Table 1)

name: Differential pair (solid state)
source: Computed by examples/harmonics_presetgen.rs (static curve projected onto T2..T9): Ideal differential pair (exponential BJT pair), y = tanh(g x), g = 1, x = v_id / (2 V_T), 2 V_T = 51.70 mV at 300 K; full-scale input 51.7 mV peak = 0 dBFS; odd orders only, no DC

name: High-feedback solid state
reference: 0 dBFS sine near full output, levels at 1 kHz
source: Archetype: a class-AB transistor amplifier with heavy global feedback and dominant-pole compensation, near full output; mostly odd orders (soft clipping of a symmetrical output stage) with a little H2, about 0.05 % THD at 1 kHz; the loop gain falls 6 dB/oct above about 2 kHz, so the residual distortion rises 6 dB/oct toward the treble (about +17 dB by 20 kHz)

name: Push-pull pentode, feedback
reference: 0 dBFS sine near full output, levels at 1 kHz
source: Archetype: a push-pull pentode output stage with moderate global feedback through an output transformer, near full output; mostly odd orders (about 0.6 % H3 at 1 kHz) with a little H2 from imbalance; the odd orders rise 12 dB/oct below about 60 Hz, up to +12 dB, as the transformer core nears saturation, and all orders rise 6 dB/oct above about 6 kHz, up to +6 dB, as the feedback falls

name: Output transformer
reference: H3 at 20 Hz for a 0 dBFS sine
source: Archetype: output transformer core saturation; core flux rises 6 dB/oct below the 100 Hz corner (H3 about 12 dB/oct), and the 12 dB boost limit flattens it below 25 Hz as the winding resistance does; about 6 % H3 at 20 Hz, 3.5 % at 40 Hz and 0.4 % at 1 kHz at full scale

name: Tape, hot
reference: H3 at 1 kHz for a 0 dBFS sine
source: Archetype: tape saturation driven hot; about 3 % H3 at 1 kHz at full scale (near maximum output level), rising about 10 dB toward the bass (about 9 % at 40 Hz) below a 400 Hz corner with a 6 dB boost limit

name: Mastering tape
reference: H3 at 1 kHz for a 0 dBFS sine
source: Archetype: well-aligned mastering tape (Jiles-Atherton hysteresis), fitted to measurements of a real reel-to-reel recorder at its maximum output level: about 3 % H3 at 1 kHz at full scale (narrow loop, width 0.25), falling about 2 dB per dB of level; a record/playback bass EQ pair (+3.5 dB below 100 Hz into the core, exact inverse after) lets the distortion rise toward the bass as measured (H3 about +8 dB at 40 Hz); a small field offset leaves only a trace of H2 (about -49 dBc at 1 kHz)

name: Studio tape
reference: H3 at 1 kHz for a 0 dBFS sine
source: Archetype: studio tape (Jiles-Atherton hysteresis) driven about 2 dB past the measured recorder's maximum output level: about 5.6 % H3 at 1 kHz at full scale (medium loop, width 0.35) with the measured level law; a record/playback bass EQ pair (+3.5 dB below 110 Hz into the core, exact inverse after) lets the distortion rise toward the bass; a moderate field offset gives H2 about -35 dBc at 1 kHz

name: Vintage tape
reference: H3 at 1 kHz for a 0 dBFS sine
source: Archetype: vintage tape (Jiles-Atherton hysteresis) driven about 4 dB past the measured recorder's maximum output level: about 9 % H3 at 1 kHz at full scale (10 % calibrated on the symmetric core; wider loop, width 0.4) with the measured level law; a record/playback bass EQ pair (+4 dB below 110 Hz into the core, exact inverse after) lets the distortion rise toward the bass; the field offset fitted to the measured machine gives H2 about -23 dBc at 1 kHz, close to H3
